excerpt: We should recognize in particular that the power of a quantum computer is not unlimited. We don’t expect, for example, that a quantum computer will be able to solve efficiently the hard instances of NP-hard problems like the traveling salesman problem. For such hard combinatorial search problems we probably can’t do much better than exhaustively searching for a solution. Quantum computers can speed up exhaustive search, but only modestly, so NP-hard problems are likely to be quantumly hard as well as classically hard.
overview: The excerpt establishes a boundary condition on quantum optimism. It matters because many commercial expectations center on optimization, yet the source explicitly warns that worst-case NP-hard search should not be expected to become easy on quantum hardware.
title: NP-Hard Limitation Argument
